mainTopic: The categories of טרפות, רבי יוחנן's rulings on the gallbladder, liver and gizzard, and holes in the layers of the gullet and gizzard
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier count of the טרפות in the משנה. עולא then teaches that all טרפות fit into eight basic types told to משה at סיני, and חייא בר רבא says the type called נקובה has eight cases. He explains that the perforated gallbladder is only the view of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. Next comes a series of rulings from רבי יוחנן. The הלכה follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה on the gallbladder, since איוב survived only by a miracle. On a removed liver, a כזית must remain, and the גמרא shows that his students report his view differently. Two more rulings follow: a pierced gallbladder sealed by the liver is kosher, and a pierced gizzard with its inner lining whole is kosher. The גמרא then discusses organs with two layers, including the gullet's red outer layer and white inner layer, and holes in both layers that do not line up. Finally רבה teaches that a scab over a hole in the gullet does not count as a covering, and that the gullet must be checked from the inside. The amud ends by asking when that last rule makes a practical difference, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Keep the two cases you removed in the count
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes its count of the משנה's טרפות by putting back the two cases it had taken out earlier.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, those two cases that you took out, do not take them out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes an earlier discussion about how to count the טרפות in the משנה. It now says that the two cases it had dropped from the count should stay in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא tried to reach the right total by removing two cases: an animal whose hind legs were cut off, and one whose hide was removed. With the new way of counting, those two cases stay in, and the total still works out.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; this word brings in a new answer that replaces the earlier one
That you took out (removed from the count)
Do not take out

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new discussion. It is the end of the counting debate from the previous lines of the daf, so 'those two' means the two cases dropped there.

phrases.english: Rather, those two that you removed,
phrases.notes: He means the two cases dropped from the count earlier: hind legs cut off, and hide removed.

phrases.english: do not remove.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָנָךְ תַּרְתֵּי דְּאַפֵּקְתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the counting discussion from just before this section
steps.terutzResolutionType: Recounting: changing which cases are included so the total matches
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two cases had to be removed for the count to work
steps.terutzMaskana: Those two cases stay in, and the count is done a different way

steps.title: עולא: Eight basic types of טרפה were given at סיני
steps.stepSummary: עולא teaches that all טרפות fall into eight basic types told to משה at סיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: Eight types of טרפות were told to משה at סיני: perforated, severed, removed, missing, torn, clawed, fallen, and broken.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא gives a new big-picture rule: every טרפה belongs to one of eight types that משה received at סיני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of a long list of single cases, עולא sorts the טרפות into eight groups. Each detailed case in the משנה, like a perforated lung or a missing organ, fits under one of these headings. Saying they were told to משה at סיני means these categories come straight from the oral tradition.

keyTerms.meaning: Animals with a fatal defect, which may not be eaten even after proper שחיטה
Were told to משה at סיני, meaning a tradition from סיני
Perforated (an organ with a hole)
Clawed, attacked by a predator
Fallen, an animal that had a bad fall

steps.whatToRemember: עולא's eight types are: נקובה, פסוקה, נטולה, חסורה, קרועה, דרוסה, נפולה, שבורה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This list became the basic framework for organizing the laws of טרפות.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
Eight types of tereifot
were told to Moses at Sinai:
perforated, severed, removed, and missing,
phrases.notes: 'Removed' means an organ that was taken out; 'missing' means one that was never there or has a piece lacking.

phrases.english: torn, clawed, fallen, and broken.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: שְׁמֹנָה מִינֵי טְרֵפוֹת נֶאֶמְרוּ לוֹ לְמֹשֶׁה בְּסִינַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new statement about how to group all the טרפות
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All טרפות fall into eight basic types from סיני

steps.title: This excludes רכיש בר פפא's diseased organ
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that עולא's list leaves out a 'diseased' organ as a type of טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is to exclude the 'diseased' case of רכיש בר פפא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what עולא's list is meant to rule out: 'diseased' is not one of the eight types.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רכיש בר פפא had said that a diseased organ (a kidney, as discussed elsewhere) makes the animal a טרפה. Since 'diseased' is not among עולא's eight, עולא does not treat that case as a טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude; to show what is left out
A diseased or damaged (struck) organ

phrases.english: To exclude the diseased organ of Rakhish bar Pappa.
phrases.notes: רכיש בר פפא said a diseased kidney is a טרפה; עולא's list leaves it out.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְאַפּוֹקֵי לָקוּתָא דְּרָכִישׁ בַּר פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the practical result of עולא's list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A diseased organ is not one of the eight types, so according to עולא it is not a טרפה

steps.title: חייא בר רבא: Eight טרפות of perforation
steps.stepSummary: חייא בר רבא says there are eight separate cases in the category of a perforated organ.
steps.simpleTranslation: חייא בר רבא said: There are eight טרפות in the category of נקובה (perforation).
steps.whatsHappening: חייא בר רבא zooms in on the first of עולא's types, נקובה, and says it contains eight cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The eight perforated organs are the gullet, brain membrane, heart, lung, abomasum, intestines, inner rumen, and the reticulum or omasum pierced to the outside. The number eight sets up a question, because the משנה seems to list a ninth.

keyTerms.meaning: In the category of a perforated organ

phrases.english: Chiyya bar Rava said:
There are eight tereifot in perforation,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר חִיָּיא בַּר רָבָא: שְׁמֹנָה טְרֵפוֹת יֵשׁ בִּנְקוּבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Breaks down the first of עולא's eight types
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The category of נקובה contains eight cases

steps.title: Why not nine? The gallbladder is one sage's view
steps.stepSummary: חייא בר רבא answers a likely question: the perforated gallbladder is not counted because only רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say there are nine, answer: the gallbladder is taught only by רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: חייא בר רבא raises a question someone might ask, 'Isn't it nine?', and answers it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה also lists a perforated gallbladder (מרה), which would make nine. חייא בר רבא explains that this case is the opinion of one sage, רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, so it is not part of the accepted count.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say; brings in a possible objection
Gallbladder
Teaches it

steps.confusionAlert: The question and the answer here come from the same speaker. This is not a separate challenge from another sage.

phrases.english: If you say nine,
phrases.notes: Nine because the משנה also lists a perforated gallbladder.

phrases.aramaic: מָרָה רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה קָתָנֵי לַהּ,
phrases.english: the gallbladder, Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda teaches it,

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם תֹּאמַר תֵּשַׁע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the number eight against the משנה's ninth case
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the extra case to a single opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The perforated gallbladder makes nine cases
steps.terutzMaskana: The gallbladder is only רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's view, so the count stays at eight

steps.title: Proof from a ברייתא that the gallbladder is a lone opinion
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that the perforated gallbladder is added only by רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: If the abomasum is perforated or the intestines are perforated, it is a טרפה. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: Even if the gallbladder is perforated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that the gallbladder case belongs to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the first opinion lists the abomasum and intestines but not the gallbladder. Only רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה adds the gallbladder with the word 'even'. This shows the gallbladder case is his own addition, which supports counting eight.

keyTerms.meaning: Abomasum, the fourth stomach
Intestines
Even; this word adds a case on top of what was said

steps.whatToRemember: The perforated gallbladder is רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's view, so חייא בר רבא counts only eight cases of נקובה.

phrases.english: As it is taught:
If the abomasum was perforated, or the intestines were perforated, it is a tereifa;
Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda says:
Even if the gallbladder was perforated.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: נִיקְּבָה הַקֵּיבָה, נִיקְּבוּ הַדַּקִּים – טְרֵפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer that the gallbladder is a single opinion
steps.raayaObject: That the perforated gallbladder is only רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's view
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where the first opinion leaves out the gallbladder and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה adds it

steps.title: Memory aid for the coming statements
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a memory aid listing key words of the statements that come next.
steps.simpleTranslation: Memory aid: הלכות, friend, olive-sized amount, gallbladder, and gizzard.
steps.whatsHappening: This line is setting up the next part of the daf. It gives a memory aid for a series of statements by רבי יצחק ברבי יוסף that are about to come.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word stands for one of the coming statements. It is not a ruling by itself, just a tool to remember the order of what follows.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid, a list of key words to help remember the coming statements
Gizzard
An olive-sized amount

phrases.english: (Halakhot, friend, olive-bulk,
phrases.notes: The round brackets here just mark a memory aid. Each word hints at one of the next statements.

phrases.english: gallbladder, and gizzard: a mnemonic).

steps.triggerLanguage: הִלְכוֹת חָבֵר כְּזַיִת מָרָה וְקוּרְקְבָן – סִימָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Transition to a new series of statements
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling; a memory aid for the statements that follow

steps.title: רבי יוחנן rules like רבי יוסי son of רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה: a perforated gallbladder makes the animal a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק ברבי יוסף said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling from רבי יוחנן on the gallbladder case it just discussed. He sides with רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5, חייא בר רבא left the perforated gallbladder off his list because only רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds it is a טרפה. Now רבי יוחנן says that this lone view is the actual הלכה. So a perforated gallbladder does make the animal a טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: The final law follows this person's opinion
A gallbladder that has a hole in it
An animal with a fatal defect, which is forbidden to eat even after proper שחיטה

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling turns a minority opinion into the practical הלכה for the gallbladder.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak son of Rabbi Yosef said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda.
phrases.notes: He means the view from step 6, that a perforated gallbladder makes the animal a טרפה.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling on the dispute shown in the ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A perforated gallbladder renders the animal a טרפה, following רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.

steps.title: The colleagues challenge from Job's gall poured out
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reports the colleagues' challenge to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה: איוב said his gall was poured out, yet he stayed alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יצחק ברבי יוסף said in the name of רבי יוחנן: What did the colleagues of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה answer him? They quoted איוב: 'He pours out my gall upon the ground,' and yet איוב was still alive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us how the other חכמים argued against רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. They pointed to איוב, who lived even though his gall was spilled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The colleagues reason that if a creature can live with a spilled gallbladder, it is not a fatal injury. A טרפה means an injury the animal cannot survive, so a perforated gallbladder should not count as one.

keyTerms.meaning: They answered him back
His colleagues, the other חכמים who disagreed with him
Gall, the bitter fluid in the gallbladder
And he was still alive

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak son of Rabbi Yosef said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
What did his colleagues answer back
to Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda?
'He pours out my gall upon the ground,'
and yet Job was still alive.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אַהְדַּרוּ לֵיהּ חַבְרֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports the main argument against the view that was just ruled as הלכה
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's view that a perforated gallbladder is a טרפה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: איוב survived a spilled gallbladder, so the injury is not fatal and should not make the animal a טרפה.

steps.title: רבי יוסי answers that a miracle is different
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה answers that איוב lived only by a miracle, and we cannot learn rules from miracles. The same verse speaks of split kidneys, and nobody survives that naturally either.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: We do not bring proof from miracles. For if you do not say this, the same verse says 'He splits my kidneys and does not spare.' Does a person live through that? Rather, a miracle is different, as it is written, 'Only guard his life.' Here too, a miracle is different.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה defends his view. He says איוב survived only because ה׳ made a miracle, so his case proves nothing about normal animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He proves this from the same verse. It also says איוב's kidneys were split, and no one naturally survives that. ה׳ had told the שטן to spare איוב's life, so his whole survival was a miracle, and the gallbladder part was a miracle too.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not bring proof from miracles
For if you do not say so (a way of showing the other side leads to a problem)
Kidneys
A miracle is different

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי does not deny that איוב lived. He agrees איוב lived, but says it was a miracle, so it teaches nothing about the normal law of טרפה.

phrases.english: He said to them:
We do not bring up miraculous events as proof,
for if you do not say so,
'He splits my kidneys and does not spare' —
does such a person live?
Rather, a miracle is different,
as it is written: 'Only guard his life.'
phrases.notes: איוב 2:6. ה׳ tells the שטן to spare איוב's life.

phrases.english: Here too, a miracle is different.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין מַזְכִּירִין מַעֲשֵׂה נִסִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the colleagues' challenge from איוב
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the proof to a miracle case that does not reflect nature
steps.terutzHavaAmina: איוב's survival shows that a perforated gallbladder is survivable
steps.terutzMaskana: איוב survived only by a miracle, as his split kidneys show, so his case does not change the law of טרפה

steps.title: רבי יוחנן rules that an olive-bulk of liver must remain
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules on the removed liver: the הלכה follows the view that a כזית of the liver must remain for the animal to be kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יצחק ברבי יוסף said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The הלכה follows the one who says a כזית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third ruling from רבי יוחנן, this time about an animal whose liver was removed. He says at least a כזית of liver has to be left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a view that a little bit of leftover liver is not enough, and a כזית must remain. רבי יוחנן says the הלכה follows that view. This ruling sets up the contradiction in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: An olive-bulk, a standard minimum amount in הלכה
Liver

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak son of Rabbi Yosef said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
The halacha follows the words of the one who says an olive-bulk.
phrases.notes: This is about a removed liver: the animal is kosher only if at least an olive's worth of liver is left.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲלָכָה כְּדִבְרֵי הָאוֹמֵר כְּזַיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling from the same chain of tradition, on a different organ
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the liver was removed, the animal is kosher only if a כזית of it remains.

steps.title: This contradicts רבי יוחנן's rule about an unattributed משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יוחנן could say this when he also rules that the הלכה follows a סתם משנה. The משנה implies that any leftover liver, even less than a כזית, is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבי יוחנן really say this? But רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The הלכה follows a סתם משנה. And we learned: If the liver was removed and nothing at all remained of it, the animal is a טרפה. This implies that if anything remained, it is kosher, even if it is less than a כזית!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ruling from step 11. It shows that another rule of רבי יוחנן points the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן holds that a משנה with no name attached is the הלכה. Our משנה says the animal is a טרפה only if nothing at all was left, which implies any leftover makes it kosher. That clashes with requiring a כזית.

keyTerms.meaning: Did he really say this? (opens a challenge from his other words)
An unattributed משנה, written with no sage's name
This implies that (drawing an inference from what the text left unsaid)
Was left over, remained

phrases.english: And did Rabbi Yochanan really say this?
But didn't Rabba bar bar Chana say
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
The halacha follows an unattributed Mishna,
and we learned in a Mishna:
If the liver was removed
and nothing at all remained of it, it is a tereifa —
this implies that if some remained, it is kosher,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא הָוֵי כְּזַיִת!
phrases.english: even though it is not an olive-bulk!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling from step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: The report that רבי יוחנן requires a כזית of liver to remain
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן follows a סתם משנה, and the סתם משנה implies any leftover amount is enough, so he could not require a כזית.

steps.title: Two אמוראים disagree about רבי יוחנן's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that two אמוראים disagree about what רבי יוחנן held, so the two reports simply reflect two different traditions.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are אמוראים, and they disagree about the view of רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction. רבי יצחק ברבי יוסף and רבה בר בר חנה report רבי יוחנן's view differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not try to make both reports fit together. It accepts that the two students hold different traditions of what רבי יוחנן said. So the contradiction is between the reporters, not inside רבי יוחנן's own words.

keyTerms.meaning: They are אמוראים (who disagree), the reports come from different sages
According to the view of, about what someone held

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן rules like רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה that a perforated gallbladder is a טרפה, since איוב's survival was a miracle. On the liver, his students disagree about his view: one reports that a כזית must remain, the other reports that he follows the סתם משנה, where any leftover is enough.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא proved one report wrong. Both reports stay, as two different traditions of רבי יוחנן's view.

phrases.english: They are Amoraim who disagree,
and they disagree about the view of Rabbi Yochanan.
phrases.notes: The two students, רבי יצחק ברבי יוסף and רבה בר בר חנה, report his view differently.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמוֹרָאֵי נִינְהוּ וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributes the two reports to a disagreement between אמוראים
steps.terutzMaskana: Two students hold different traditions of רבי יוחנן's view, so there is no self-contradiction

steps.title: A pierced gallbladder that the liver seals is kosher
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that if the gallbladder (מרה) has a hole and the liver (כבד) blocks it, the animal stays kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק ברבי יוסף said in the name of רבי יוחנן: if the gallbladder got a hole and the liver closes it up, the animal is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ruling of רבי יוחנן about a gallbladder with a hole in it. If the liver plugs the hole, the animal is kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, for רבי יוחנן, a pierced gallbladder makes the animal a טרפה. Here the liver lies right against the hole and seals it, so the hole is treated as closed and the animal is כשרה.

keyTerms.meaning: The gallbladder
Got a hole in it, was pierced
The liver
Seals it, blocks up the hole
Kosher, fit to eat

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yitzchak son of Rabbi Yosef said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
A gallbladder that got a hole,
phrases.notes: The hole is in the spot where the gallbladder touches the liver.

phrases.english: and the liver seals it, the animal is kosher.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the discussion about the liver, the גמרא moves to another ruling of רבי יוחנן about a pierced gallbladder.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A pierced gallbladder whose hole is sealed by the liver is kosher.

steps.title: A pierced gizzard with its inner lining whole is kosher
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that if a bird's gizzard (קורקבן) is pierced but its inner lining (כיס) is still whole, the bird is kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יצחק ברבי יוסף said in the name of רבי יוחנן: if the gizzard got a hole but its inner lining is still whole, the bird is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a second ruling from the same chain of names. A hole in the outer flesh of the gizzard does not make the bird treif as long as the inner lining has no hole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The gizzard has two parts: the thick outer flesh and a thin inner lining, the כיס. Since the inner lining still holds the food in, the bird stays כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: The gizzard, a bird's second stomach
The inner lining (literally, the pouch) of the gizzard
Whole, still intact

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak son of Rabbi Yosef said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
If the gizzard got a hole but its inner lining is whole,
it is kosher.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ruling from the same chain of names, now about the gizzard.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A gizzard pierced in its outer flesh, with the inner lining whole, is kosher.

steps.title: What if only the inner lining is pierced?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about the opposite case: the inner lining has a hole, but the gizzard's outer flesh is whole.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: if the inner lining got a hole but the gizzard itself is whole, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question that flips the last case around. Now the inner lining is pierced and the outer flesh is whole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן only told us that an intact inner lining saves the bird. We still don't know whether an intact outer flesh can do the same job.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them, an open question
What is the law?

phrases.english: A question was asked among them:
If the inner lining got a hole but the gizzard is whole,
what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: נִיקַּב הַכִּיס וְקוּרְקְבָן קַיָּים, מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the reverse of the case in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a bird kosher if only the inner lining of its gizzard is pierced and the outer flesh is whole?

steps.title: רב נחמן: one layer pierced without the other is kosher
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רב נחמן's rule: if one layer is pierced without the other, the animal is kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, for רב נחמן said: if this layer got a hole without that one, it is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a statement of רב נחמן. Whenever only one of two layers is pierced, the animal is kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן's words do not say which layer has the hole. That shows the inner layer being pierced alone is just as fine as the outer layer being pierced alone.

keyTerms.meaning: This one without that one, only one of the two layers

phrases.english: Come and hear,
for Rav Nachman said:
If this one got a hole without that one, it is kosher.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to answer the question in step 16.
steps.raayaObject: That the bird is kosher even if only the inner lining is pierced.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב נחמן's rule that a hole in one layer without the other is kosher, with no difference between the layers.

steps.title: רבא: the gullet has two layers, red outside and white inside
steps.stepSummary: רבא teaches that the gullet (ושט) has two layers, a red outer one and a white inner one. If only one of them is pierced, the animal is kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the gullet has two layers, the outer one red and the inner one white. If this one got a hole without that one, it is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a similar statement from רבא about the gullet. A hole through only one of its two layers does not make the animal treif.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same idea as רב נחמן's rule, now spelled out for the ושט. רבא adds the colors of each layer, and the next step asks why he bothered to mention them.

keyTerms.meaning: The gullet, the food pipe
Skins, layers
Outer
Inner

phrases.english: Rava said:
The gullet has two layers,
the outer one red and the inner one white;
if this one got a hole without that one, it is kosher.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: שְׁנֵי עוֹרוֹת יֵשׁ לוֹ לַוֶּושֶׁט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel statement that supports the same idea as רב נחמן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A gullet pierced through only one of its two layers is kosher.

steps.title: Why mention the colors?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבא needed to say that the outer layer is red and the inner one is white.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need him to say that the outer one is red and the inner one is white?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask about an extra detail in רבא's words. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The colors look like plain anatomy that has nothing to do with the law. The גמרא assumes רבא would not add a detail unless it teaches something.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need to say it?

phrases.english: Why do I need to say
the outer one red and the inner one white?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמָה לִי לְמֵימַר חִיצוֹן אָדוֹם וּפְנִימִי לָבָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about an extra detail in רבא's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What law do the colors in רבא's statement teach?

steps.title: If the colors are switched, the animal is treif
steps.stepSummary: The colors teach that if the layers are switched, with a white outer layer and a red inner one, the animal is a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because if they are switched, it is treif.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the colors are a sign of a healthy gullet. If the colors are reversed, the animal is treif.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The detail that looked like extra description turns out to be a real law. A gullet with its colors switched is not normal, and that alone makes the animal a טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: Switched, swapped around
An animal with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat

phrases.english: Because if they are switched, it is treif.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי חַלֵּיף – טְרֵפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The colors are given because a gullet with switched colors is a טרפה.

steps.title: Both layers pierced, but the holes don't line up
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if both layers have holes, but the holes are not across from each other, what is the law?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: if both layers got holes, but not across from each other, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new question. Both layers are pierced, but the two holes are in different spots.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now one layer was always whole. Here neither layer is whole, but there is still no hole that goes straight through, so the case is unclear.

keyTerms.meaning: Not across from each other, the holes don't line up
What is the law?

phrases.english: A question was asked among them:

phrases.aramaic: נִיקְּבוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם זֶה שֶׁלֹּא כְּנֶגֶד זֶה,
phrases.english: If both got holes, not across from each other,
what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: נִיקְּבוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם זֶה שֶׁלֹּא כְּנֶגֶד זֶה, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the two-layer rule with a harder case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is an organ with both layers pierced, at different spots, kosher?

steps.title: מר זוטרא: kosher in the gullet, unfit in the gizzard
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא, in the name of רב פפא, answers that in the gullet it is kosher, but in the gizzard it is unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said in the name of רב פפא: in the gullet it is kosher; in the gizzard it is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא gives an answer that splits the two organs. The gullet is kosher and the gizzard is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His answer treats the two organs differently, but it does not give a reason. רב אשי will argue in the next step that the logic should go the other way.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of
Unfit, not kosher

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Mar Zutra said in the name of Rav Pappa:
In the gullet, it is kosher;
in the gizzard, it is unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Holes that don't line up are kosher in the gullet and unfit in the gizzard.

steps.title: רב אשי: it should be the other way around
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי argues that the opposite makes more sense. The gullet stretches and shrinks, so its holes can come to line up, while the gizzard always stays still.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי challenged it: Just the opposite! The gullet, which the animal eats with and calls out with, is roomy; it squeezes it and stretches it, so sometimes the holes line up with each other. The gizzard rests in place and stays just as it is!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי attacks מר זוטרא's answer. He says the gullet should be the dangerous one and the gizzard the safe one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The gullet keeps moving when the animal eats and makes sounds, so two holes that start apart can slide into line and make one hole straight through. The gizzard does not move, so holes that don't line up will never line up.

keyTerms.meaning: Challenged it, raised a strong objection
On the contrary, just the opposite
Squeezes it, makes it smaller
Stretches it out
Line up, match up with each other

phrases.english: Rav Ashi challenged it:
Just the opposite! The gullet,
which the animal eats with and calls out with,
is roomy; it squeezes it and stretches it,
so sometimes the holes line up with each other.
The gizzard, which rests in place,
stays just as it is!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אָשֵׁי: אַדְּרַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: מר זוטרא's ruling that the gullet is kosher and the gizzard is unfit.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The gullet moves all the time, so its holes can come to line up. The gizzard stays still, so its holes never will. The ruling should be reversed.

steps.title: The correct report of מר זוטרא matches רב אשי
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב יוסף tells רב אשי that the right version of מר זוטרא's words, in the name of רב פפא, actually agrees with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא the son of רב יוסף said to רב אשי: this is how we say it in the name of מר זוטרא, that he said in the name of רב פפא just like you.
steps.whatsHappening: The argument ends with a correction of the tradition. מר זוטרא really said what רב אשי thinks: in the gullet it is unfit, and in the gizzard it is kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is not solved by a new reason. The report of מר זוטרא's words is simply fixed. So the final law is the reverse of step 22: holes that don't line up make the gullet unfit but leave the gizzard kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: This is how we say it, this is our version
Like you, in agreement with you

steps.whatToRemember: Two holes that don't line up: in the ושט, which moves, the animal is a טרפה, because the holes may come to line up. In the קורקבן, which stays still, the bird is kosher. This is the corrected version of מר זוטרא's words, which matches רב אשי.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't remember the first version from step 22 as the law. It was corrected, and the final ruling is the reverse.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha the son of Rav Yosef said to Rav Ashi:
This is how we say it in the name of Mar Zutra,
that he said in the name of Rav Pappa just like you.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי אָמְרִינַן מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּמָר זוּטְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles רב אשי's challenge by correcting the report of מר זוטרא's words.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the tradition of what was said
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: If both layers are pierced at different spots, the gullet is unfit and the gizzard is kosher.

steps.title: A scab over a wound in the gullet is not a real membrane
steps.stepSummary: רבה rules that a קרום that grew because of a מכה in the וושט does not count as a קרום.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה said: A skin that grew because of a wound in the gullet is not considered a real skin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ruling from רבה: if a thin skin grows over a hole in the וושט, it does not count as a covering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a covering could seem to close up a hole. רבה teaches that a skin that grew only because of an injury is weak and does not fix the hole. So the hole is still treated as a real hole, and the animal is a טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: A thin skin or membrane
A wound or injury
The gullet, the food pipe
An animal with a fatal defect that may not be eaten

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the new skin "heals" the hole. רבה's whole point is that this kind of skin does not count, so the hole is still there in הלכה.

phrases.english: And Rabba said:
A membrane that grew because of a wound
in the gullet is not a membrane.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבָּה: קְרוּם שֶׁעָלָה מֵחֲמַת מַכָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new statement of רבה about the וושט, after the discussion of holes in the two layers ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A membrane formed over a wound in the וושט does not count as a covering, so the hole still makes the animal a טרפה.

steps.title: The gullet must be checked from the inside
steps.stepSummary: רבה rules that the וושט cannot be checked from the outside, only from the inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה said: The gullet cannot be checked from the outside, only from the inside.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives a second ruling: when checking the וושט for damage, you must look at it from the inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We learned earlier that the outer layer of the וושט is red and the inner layer is white. Redness from an injury cannot be seen against a red layer, but it shows up clearly on the white inner layer. So a real בדיקה must be done from the inside.

keyTerms.meaning: Checking or inspecting for a defect
From the outside
On the inside

phrases.english: And Rabba said:
The gullet has no checking from the outside,
phrases.notes: Remember from step 18: the outer layer is red, so injury redness won't show there.

phrases.english: only from the inside.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבָּה: וֶושֶׁט אֵין לוֹ בְּדִיקָה מִבַּחוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ruling of רבה about the וושט, placed right after his first one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The וושט must be inspected from the inside, not the outside.

steps.title: What practical difference does this rule make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks in what case it actually matters that the וושט is checked from the inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the practical difference of this rule?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks when רבה's rule about checking from the inside actually makes a difference. This is a setup question; the answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה's rule sounds clear, but the גמרא wants to know in which real case someone would need to check the וושט this way. The question prepares us for a specific case where the rule changes the outcome.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference comes out of this?

phrases.english: For what does it make a difference?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאי נָפְקָא מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the practical use of רבה's ruling in step 26.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what case does it matter that the וושט must be checked from the inside rather than the outside?
